title: unified-rollouts: enhance rollback observability and add e2e tests for autorollback
author: Amina Patel
release_notes: Added rollout rollback observability metrics, per-rollout timeline traces, and e2e stability tests for autorollback. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: production autorollback workflows for unified rollouts have limited visibility into why a rollback was triggered and lacked deterministic e2e coverage. This PR adds richer telemetry, per-rollout timeline traces, improved alerting hooks, and a deterministic e2e test harness that validates quarantine and auto-rollback paths under synthetic metric degradation. Summary of changes: 1) telemetry: emit rollout_event and rollback_reason events with tags (rollout_id, policy, metric_snapshot, timeline_id); 2) traces: record per-rollout timeline spans to tracing backend and surface a human-readable timeline in Rollouts UI; 3) alerts: add new alert rules for unexpected rollback quorums and prolonged quarantine; 4) e2e: tests that simulate canary and shadow traffic with injected metric regressions to validate automatic rollback and manual quarantine; 5) stability guards: add backoff and minimum-observation-window gating to reduce spurious rollbacks. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-2245) - [x] metrics schema and docs updated - [x] tracing spans instrumented - [x] unit tests added - [x] deterministic e2e tests added and flake-reduced - [x] safety guard: min-observation-window implemented - [x] ops runbook updated How to test: run unit and integration suite locally (make test), run e2e harness via scripts/e2e/run_rollouts_e2e.sh which supports deterministic seeding of synthetic metrics, verify events in telemetry (events.redwood.rollout) and traces in Zipkin/OTel. Rollout plan: staged rollout to staging, enable feature flag rollout.observability_v2, monitor telemetry/dashboard for 48h, then release to canary and finally global. Related: ENG-2310 implements rollout-quorum metric; SUP-4123 is support ticket that motivated improved rollback for a live incident. No breaking API changes.
